newsitem.title: UK: Oil prices slip as gasoline falters, Iraq oil flows.
newsitem.headline: Oil prices slip as gasoline falters, Iraq oil flows.

text.p: World oil prices fell on Friday as a bout of profit-taking swept through the market at the end of a week of climbing prices.
Faltering gasoline demand and the first exports of oil from Iraq also weighed on prices.
World benchmark Brent blend crude was down 12 cents at $18.94 at 1449 GMT, near the middle of the range traded over the past six months.
"Gasoline has run out of steam a little bit and there was also some profit-taking," said Charles Gray of Prudential Bache Futures in London.
Summer demand for gasoline in the United States, tightness in Europe and a rash of technical probelms at refineries have helped buoy world oil prices in recent weeks.
But a seasonal fall in demand in the West appeared to more than offset support from low stocks and the prospect of extra autumn demand from Nigeria.
Although Nigeria is by far Africa's biggest oil producer, it is having to import oil because of the poor state of its refineries, resulting in acute fuel shortages.
The problem is exacerbated by squabbles between government ministries about how to pay for repairs.
The growing tide of Iraqi exports piled downward pressure on prices despite a nine percent month-on-month fall in the main North Sea oil loadings.
The first tanker to load Iraqi oil under the second stage of the United Nations oil-for-food deal was due to leave the Turkish port of Ceyhan at 1000 GMT on Friday, a Turkish pipeline official said.

The next tanker was due to berth just one hour after the first tanker leaves. This will be followed by a flurry of 17 further vessels due to load this month as Iraq chases a cash target of $1 billion of oil sales by September 5.
The renewed Iraqi crude exports are mostly heading West and are competing with recent sales of crude from German strategic stocks.
The extra crude from those two sources is tending to keep refiners, eager to pick off distressed cargoes, away from buying prompt oil.
